pagerbot: PAGER: [P0] GPU pool 'priority-gpu-pool' queue-growth > 8k, request throttling at 429, autoscaler failing to provision new nodes (see runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/gpu-autoscale). Oncall: @Ena

Ena (oncall): I'm on it — looking at console now. Dashboard shows sustained queue growth and 95% pool utilization. Any obvious recent deploys?

Mike R: Not seeing deploys in the last 30m. I'm seeing a spike in CUDA/Xid errors and kernel OOMs on a subset of nodes: gpu-node-{12,17,21}. Logs show repeated Xid 31, GPU HANGs, then nodes go NotReady.

Alisha K: Autoscaler is hitting API rate limits from the cloud side and our maxNodes is set to 50 for that pool. Current desired is 50, actual 50, and there's a backlog. We also have multiple nodes flapping which reduces effective capacity.

Taylor S: Posting a tail of the driver errors from gpu-node-17: 
```
[2026-03-14T22:11:58Z] nvidia: Xid (31): GpuHang detected on GPU 0
[2026-03-14T22:12:03Z] kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 24321 (python) total-vm:34G
[2026-03-14T22:12:05Z] nvidia: GPU 0: GPU reset succeeded
[2026-03-14T22:12:09Z] nvidia: Xid (31): GpuHang repeated
```

Mike R: Those resets are causing the node to flake out of the kubelet healthchecks and then the autoscaler treats them as unhealthy. We get a churn loop: flapping -> removed -> capacity down -> queue grow -> autoscaler tries to add nodes -> API rate limit / quota / maxNodes prevents growth -> customers hit 429s.

Ena (oncall): Immediate mitigation plan?

Alisha K: Short term: 1) Temporarily increase pool maxNodes to 80 (cloud request in progress) 2) Enable fallback routing for non-critical traffic to lower-tier model endpoints to relieve pressure 3) Drain and isolate nodes showing Xid errors and roll driver back on a small canary subset.

Sam G: I'll message cloud infra to lift the autoscaler quota and watch for rate limit windows. Filed ticket with cloud provider support (INC-1998). ETA ~ 10-15m.

Taylor S: I'm going to cordon + drain gpu-node-17 now and move workloads off. Command: 
```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-17
kubectl drain gpu-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

Mike R: After draining, I pulled the driver stack details. Installed driver 535.113.01 on those nodes in the last week; there are known regressions with that patchset on some kernel combos. Rolling back to 525.89.05 on a canary node.

Ena (oncall): Alisha, confirm when maxNodes bump is done and whether autoscaler is able to create nodes.

Alisha K: Cloud support increased quota and we updated autoscaler maxNodes to 80. Autoscaler logs show new node creation starting — provisioning succeeded for 2 nodes but some provisioning attempts are failing with the same driver crash symptom once GPU driver loads. So provisioners spin but effective capacity not increasing proportionally.

runtime-bot: NOTE: temporary routing rule applied: route non-critical model calls to 'small-variant' pool. Expected reduction in queue ~30%.

Customer-ops: Notifying top 5 affected customers per escalation playbook. Draft message: "We're investigating increased latency and throttling against GPU-backed endpoints, mitigations in progress. We'll update in 30 minutes."

Ena (oncall): Can we reduce burst pressure by throttling lower priority routes?

Taylor S: Yes implemented per-route rate-limits for dev and non-enterprise keys via gateway. That cut incoming rate to the pool by ~22%.

Mike R: Driver rollback on canary node (gpu-node-99) completed and node stable for 6m. Observed no Xid events after rollback. Steps taken: 
1) cordon node-99
2) apt remove nvidia-driver-535*; install nvidia-driver-525.89.05
3) restart kubelet + nvidia-container-runtime
4) uncordon once stable

Alisha K: Rolling this rollback to three more drained nodes now, will batch at 2 nodes at a time to avoid capacity dips.

Ena (oncall): Any change in queue or customer impact?

Alisha K: After the combined actions (maxNodes bump + routing + per-route throttle + driver rollback on canaries), queue size dropped from 8.1k to 1.6k over 20 minutes. Throttle rate for premium customers reduced from 18% to ~4%. Some batch jobs still queued.

Customer-ops: Sent update to customers: short note and link to status page. No SLA breaches yet but we are monitoring closely.

Sam G: Cloud provider confirmed driver bug patterns with driver 535.* on the host kernel we use. They're recommending pinning to 525.x until vendor patch. Logged for infra upgrade.

Taylor S: Creating a short-term autoscaler policy tweak: increase stableWindow and backoff tolerance to avoid overreacting to flapping nodes. Patching now.

Ena (oncall): Who owns postmortem and RCA?

Mike R: I will pair with runtime team (Taylor) to produce a postmortem. Initial notes: root cause is driver regression (535.x) causing GPU hangs and OOMs on certain kernels which led to effective capacity drop and autoscaler oscillation plus autoscaler quota + rate limits preventing quick recovery. Secondary contributing: lack of automated driver-health gating during node reprovision.

Alisha K: Open action items: 
- [P0] Rollback remaining affected nodes to 525.89.05 (in progress)
- [P1] Add driver gating in node provisioning pipeline (need infra change)
- [P1] Autoscaler: raise default maxNodes for high-priority pools + improve rate-limit backoff logic
- [P2] Postmortem + customer blameless summary

Ena (oncall): Marking incident as mitigated for now. We'll keep the thread open for the next hour to ensure stability. Good job team. :thumbsup:

pagerbot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Mitigation applied, queue decreased, driver rollback in progress. Incident severity remains P1 until postmortem.

Mike R: I'll start the postmortem draft and link logs + timelines. Leaving notes for longer-term fix: automated driver canary before large scale driver upgrades, alert on Xid surge as a first-class signal.

Ena (oncall): Handoff: I'll create an entry in the incident tracker, assign to Mike R and Taylor S for RCA and to Alisha for infra follow-ups. If anything regresses, page the oncall again immediately.

customer-ops: Sent another update to customers with ETA for full recovery ~2-3 hours while we finish rolling rollback across the pool.

Mike R: Last check — queue stable at 1.4k, premium throttle ~3.8%, nodes stable after second rollback batch. Setting last_message_ts now.

Ena (oncall): Thanks all — closing active paging.
